Liz — thanks for the clear list. Summary below (high level) with attachments and links. Happy to hop on a short call if you prefer to walk through.

Executive summary (short):
- Data plane (inference serving): target RTO 15 minutes for warm-standby regional failover; measured RTO in last full rehearsal = 12 minutes for traffic restore to regional replicas. RPO: <1 minute for request logs and telemetry (near-sync replication to durable storage), model KV caches are rebuildable (RPO best-effort).
- Control plane (management/orchestration): target RTO 60 minutes for full control-plane recovery; partial admin functions available within 10–20 minutes depending on route failovers. Measured in rehearsal = 38 minutes to restore full control-plane admin functions.
- Customer configuration and artifacts: continuous replication to durable object store (multi-region S3-compatible), daily snapshots of stateful customer metadata + 30-day point-in-time retention for configs; backups stored encrypted at rest with versioning. RPO for configs: configurable by customer (default: 15 minutes for hosted; Dedicated can request stricter guarantees).
- Backups: daily full snapshots (00:00 UTC), incremental snapshots every 6 hours, and continuous write-ahead replication for critical metadata. Retention: 30/90/365-day policy options depending on contract.
- Cross-region failover: automated traffic routing to warm replicas managed by our routing layer (health checks + circuit-breaker). DNS TTLs are pre-warmed; typical DNS cutover completes within one TTL cycle (60s–120s) plus routing propagation — end-to-end traffic restoration measured within the RTO windows above. Model artifacts are replicated asynchronously but prioritized during failover; model download and cache warm-up executed as part of the orchestrated failover (adds a minute or two depending on model size).

Evidence attached: bcdr_runbook_v1.3.pdf (runbook extract), failover_test_report_20270415.zip (logs and raw outputs). I've also linked the shared runbook folder for your convenience.

Notes / optional SLA: For Dedicated customers we support contract-level RPO/RTO commitments (can include <5 minute RPO for metadata via synchronous replication and prioritized failover paths).

If you want the post-mortem and measured timings rather than zipped logs, I can pull the summarized PDF.

Liz — thanks for the follow-ups. Attached is a concise package and quick answers inline.

- Measured timings (2027-04-15 full rehearsal, data plane switchover):
  a) Time to route customer traffic to regional replica: median = 12 minutes (95th pctile = 19 minutes) — includes DNS propagation, health-check stabilization and routing convergence.
  b) Time until critical background jobs (snapshot finalization, replication catch-up): median = 24 minutes; in the test large snapshot catch-up completed in 27 minutes. We include a prioritized catch-up queue in the orchestrator to expedite critical metadata syncs.

- Metadata/config RPO details: default hosted configuration provides near-minute granularity via frequent incremental snapshots plus write-ahead logs stored in multi-region durable storage. Recovery is effectively point-in-time to the minute (PITR at ~1 minute granularity). Customers that need transaction-level PITR can be enabled on Dedicated via synchronous replication to a hot standby.

- Dedicated <5 minute RPO add-on: This is an architecture option using synchronous replication and reserved networking between primary and hot-standby regions. Typical cost levers: additional reserved GPUs for the hot-standby (charged as a percent of committed capacity), dedicated network egress and cross-region replication charges, and higher operational support tier (on-call overlap). Ballpark uplift: +15–35% of baseline Dedicated cost depending on model footprint and Replica sizing. We include formal pricing in our Dedicated SOWs.

Attached artifacts: failover_test_summary_20270415.pdf (one-page measured timings + charts), replication_topology_diagram.png (high-level topology), dr_rehearsal_slides_202703.pdf. The original raw logs are in the ZIP if you want the full dataset.
